add_block.new_heading: What goes on a suhoor menu in Dubai?
new_paragraphs: A strong suhoor menu in Dubai leans on slow-releasing, hydrating foods that hold you through the fast — not the rich, heavy plates that suit iftar. Our chefs build around complex carbohydrates, protein and fibre. Expect overnight oats and chia bowls, foul medames and hummus, labneh with olive oil, wholegrain and cheese manakish, shakshuka, grilled halloumi, and eggs done to order. Fresh fruit, dates, laban and freshly pressed juices keep hydration up. Lighter mains and sides round out the table. Every menu is fully bespoke and prepared halal by default. Treat these as starting points we tailor to your taste, your guests and any allergies. Want indulgence too? We can add a dessert or a coffee-and-tea service. The balance is yours to set.

add_block.new_heading: The suhoor menu in Dubai, course by course
new_paragraphs: Below is the working list a chef builds your suhoor menu from, set out in the order the table is laid. Suhoor is breakfast-shaped. Treating it as a lighter iftar is the most common mistake in this city, and it shows at 3am when nobody wants a lamb ouzi. Every section is a pick-list: you choose from it, the chef sizes each course to your numbers, and anything can be swapped. Volume formats run from a minimum of 10 guests, or 20 for a buffet.
The cold table — set before anyone sits down
Laid out first and left standing through the meal, so whoever wakes late still eats properly instead of waiting on a kitchen.
Labneh salad and labneh with mint — thick, salted, flooded with olive oil
Assorted cheese selection — akkawi, halloumi and shanklish rolled in thyme
Makdous — baby aubergines cured with walnut and chilli, kept under oil
Olive salad — cracked green olives with lemon and garlic
Hummus , moutabal and mohammara
Vine leaves , rolled cold with rice, tomato and lemon
Tabbouleh and fattoush , dressed at the last minute so the bread stays sharp
Assorted jams with fresh Arabic bread
The hot breakfast table — cooked in the small hours
This is the part that has to land hot, minutes before you sit. It is timed backward from the adhan, not from the clock.
Foul medammes with tomato, onion and tahina sauce, brought out in the pot
Hummus balila — warm whole chickpeas with cumin, lemon and olive oil
Eggs of choice , cooked to order at the stove, not held in a warming tray
Shakshuka with red bell pepper and tomato
Fatteh with yoghurt — toasted bread under chickpeas, yoghurt and pine nuts
Chicken liver , seared sharp with lemon
Balaleet — sweet saffron vermicelli under a thin plain omelette, the Emirati pre-dawn plate
Chebab with date syrup — the saffron-and-cardamom Emirati pancake, off the griddle
Seasonal fruit with honeyed yoghurt
The saj station, run live
Dough rolled thin and baked in front of guests on a domed saj griddle. This is the one item worth staying awake for, and it is the reason a suhoor table beats a delivery bag.
Manakeesh zaatar , manakeesh cheese and manakeesh kishek
Lahem beajine — minced lamb with tomato and pine nuts on flatbread
Fatayer akkawi cheese , fatayer zaatar and cheese , fatayer meat and cheese
Nutella flatbread , folded straight off the saj

Live stations are quoted as discrete units with a stated capacity — a set number of pieces off the saj, a set number of kunafa buns — and that station price includes the chef running it and the setup, which plain buffet dishes do not. It makes the theatre a line you can see and price, not a vague upsell.

Where the saj goes is decided by its fuel. An electric saj dome needs no fuel approval, so it runs in a villa kitchen, on a villa terrace, or inside an apartment on a socket with headroom — which matters at 3am, when most of this city eats suhoor at home. A gas saj stays outdoors and at ground level at a villa, because the UAE Fire Code keeps LPG cylinders out of indoor spaces (11-2.2.6) and off roofs and terraces (Table 11.1), and Emaar's vertical-community rules bar residents from bringing a cylinder into a tower or a unit. On a yacht neither version comes aboard: D-Marin Art. 53.1(a) allows only the vessel's own installed gas supply, and Dubai Harbour section 7.4 prohibits operating gas cylinders on marina premises. For a suhoor on the water the manakeesh and fatayer bake in the licensed kitchen, travel warm and wrapped, and the live part becomes a fill-and-fold counter on deck. On a rooftop or at a desert camp, myCHEF confirms the setup with the building management or the site before quoting.
The South Asian suhoor table
Not a sub-section in Dubai — for a great many households it is the whole menu. Chosen instead of the Levantine table, or set alongside it.
Thalassery chicken biryani and Thalassery mutton biryani — the short-grain Malabar version, not a Hyderabadi one
Der raat ki mutton nihari and beef nihari — braised through the night and finished at suhoor, the dish literally built for this hour
Haleem , pounded to a paste, ladled with fried onion and ginger
Malabar chicken khorma and chicken pulao
Thari kanji — the Kerala rice-and-vermicelli porridge, the gentlest thing on the table
Daal , mix pakora and vegetable samosa
Chana chaat , dahi bhalla and raitha
Paratha , coin paratha , nice pathiri and assorted rotis
Papad, pickle and chutney , with fresh mint chutney
Desserts, deliberately lighter than iftar
Luqaimat with date syrup — fried to order and eaten hot
Cheese kunafah , pulled hot from a live kunefe plate
Umm Ali
Arabic delight selection
Drinks — the Ramadan list, not the standard one
What separates a suhoor beverage list from any other is that it carries the drinks of the season, not a default run of soft drinks and orange juice.
Jallab with pine nuts and raisins, and qamar al-din apricot
Vimto and Rooh Afza
Laban , chilled, and fresh juices — orange, mango, strawberry, pineapple, lemon mint
Karak tea , gahwa from a live Arabic-coffee station, and sulaimani with lemon and mint
Mocktails, tea and coffee, mineral water
Suhoor and snack boxes, for teams and community programmes

A separate product line from the buffet, tiered and itemised, for offices running late Ramadan shifts, staff welfare programmes and community distribution. Contents are listed line by line so you can see what a tier upgrade buys.
Basic box — chicken or mutton biryani
Standard box — biryani, laban or juice, one fruit, 3 dates and water
Premium box — biryani, fruit, laban or juice, water and 3 dates
Royal box — the premium contents plus samosa and pakora
Full-meal box — snack or soup, a veg or non-veg main, rice, fresh salad, raita, assorted rotis, papad pickle and chutney, and dessert
Snack boxes and fruit platters for a lighter pre-dawn drop
Dietary options on the suhoor menu

Vegetarian and vegan choices sit throughout the cold table, the saj list and the South Asian table, and the whole menu is prepared halal by default. Gluten-free, nut-conscious and other dietary menu options may be available on request, subject to confirmation by the assigned culinary partner. Partner kitchens may handle allergens, and cross-contact cannot be completely excluded unless dedicated controls have been specifically confirmed for the booking. Guests with allergies must provide full details before confirming their event.

add_block.new_heading: When is Ramadan 2026, and when do suhoor dates fill?
new_paragraphs: Ramadan 2026 is expected to begin on 18 or 19 February, subject to the official moon sighting. Khaleej Times reports 18 February; Gulf News reports 19 February. add_block.new_heading: Where to go for suhoor in Dubai, or host it at home
new_paragraphs: Where to go for suhoor in Dubai has two honest answers. The first is a suhoor restaurant or a hotel tent. The city runs late Ramadan sittings across hotels, majlis tents and cafes. Each holds its tables to a set time and a set menu. It suits a night out with friends. It needs no planning beyond the reservation. The second is your own table, which is where myCHEF works. A chef arrives, cooks the pre-dawn meal in your kitchen, serves it and clears before Fajr. The family eats at the hour the fast sets, not the hour a venue does.

We publish no list of the best suhoor restaurant in Dubai. A ranking of other people's venues, written by a caterer, is worth nothing to you. What we can tell you is which format suits which night. A large family, or any group with children, eats better at home: the room is quiet and nobody drives at 3am. A small group with no host duties has a good night out. Elderly guests, and anyone praying Fajr at home, are better served by a table already laid where they are.

new_paragraphs: How much does suhoor catering cost in Dubai?

It starts at AED 90 per person for a dropped-off or boxed suhoor, AED 120 for a staffed buffet and AED 150 for a premium table with live saj and kunafa stations. A chef cooking and serving on site is AED 700 to 950 per person. Minimums are 10 guests on volume formats, 20 on a buffet and AED 900 on order value, and packages run from AED 1,200 to 5,500 for larger multi-station events.
What's included in suhoor catering?
Menu design, a vetted chef cooking on site, service staff where needed, plating, setup and full cleanup are all included. You host; we handle the food and the room.
How far ahead should I book suhoor catering?

As guidance: 72 hours for a standard package, 3 to 5 days with live stations or multi-staff service, and 5 to 7 days for a bespoke menu or a larger private event. Ramadan is the exception, because the dates are fixed and shared by the whole city, so send a Ramadan night as far ahead as you can. Short-notice requests are assessed individually.
Is the suhoor menu halal?
Yes — every suhoor menu is prepared halal by default, and partners source and cook accordingly. Vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free and other dietary options are all standard.
Can you do corporate suhoor catering for a large team?
Yes — corporate suhoor catering in Dubai scales from boardroom plates to hundred-guest buffets and individually boxed options for hybrid teams. We scale staff to the room.
Do you offer a private suhoor chef for one household?
Yes — a private suhoor chef in Dubai serves a single family table, keeping the footprint small and quiet, cooking fresh and clearing away before Fajr.
Can I get a suhoor menu tailored to my taste?
Every menu is bespoke. Share your preferences and any dietary needs, and the chef designs a suhoor menu around your guests, not a fixed template.
Where can I go for suhoor in Dubai?

Two options. Hotels, majlis tents and cafes across the city run late suhoor sittings through Ramadan, at a set time and a set menu. Or the meal comes to you. A chef cooks suhoor in your own kitchen and clears before Fajr, which suits families, older guests and anyone staying off the roads at 3am.
When does Ramadan 2026 begin?

Ramadan 2026 is expected to begin on 18 or 19 February, subject to the official moon sighting. Suhoor and iftar dates fill across the whole month, and weekends and the last ten nights go first, so send your date before the month opens.
What is the leading catering company in Dubai?

No single company leads catering in Dubai, and any company claiming the title is claiming it about itself. The market splits between hotel catering arms, high-volume buffet operators and chef-led services like myCHEF. Judge on what a caterer will tell you before you enquire: published per-head prices, a minimum headcount, a minimum order value, a named chef and an itemised quote. Ours are printed on this page, and our guide to choosing a catering company in Dubai sets out the checks.
Do you cater iftar as well as suhoor?

Yes. Iftar opens the fast at sunset and suhoor closes the night before dawn, and the menus differ. Booking both with one chef keeps the planning in one place; our iftar catering page covers the sunset meal, including iftar home catering.
For suhoor catering, the chefs and partner kitchens handling your booking operate to Dubai Municipality food-safety requirements .
